rows.title: CT created a $34M COVID relief fund for essential workers. It remains largely unspent.
rows.standfirst: The state has awarded just 1.1% of the $34 million budget for the Essential Workers COVID-19 Assistance Program since it launched.

rows.title: Lamont: Pouring budget surpluses into pensions means big savings next year
rows.standfirst: CT used billions of budget surplus dollars to pay down pension debt, freeing up $440 million annually to use for other programs.

rows.title: Report: CT never came up with a plan to collect more online sales tax
rows.standfirst: State auditors say the tax department never fulfilled a 2019 directive to come up with a plan to secure $30 million from online transactions.

rows.title: CT budget surplus shatters the $4B mark
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s $4.3 billion budget surplus allows the state to make a huge payment against longstanding pension debt.

rows.title: Only half of eligible households have claimed CT’s $250-per-child tax rebate
rows.standfirst: The child tax rebate is available to single parents who earned $100,000 or less and to couples who make $200,000 or less.

rows.title: Bob Stefanowski would tap CT’s reserves to aid small businesses
rows.standfirst: Bob Stefanowski’s $640 million relief plan would tap CT’s rainy day fund to help small businesses replenish the unemployment trust.

rows.title: West Haven could lose grants, credit rating amid financial scandal
rows.standfirst: West Haven has been effectively cut out of grants from CT’s State Bond Commission, an indication of the extent of the city’s fiscal problems.

rows.title: CT bond panel OKs $850M in finance, including $60M for local projects
rows.standfirst: The State Bond Commission approved more than $60 million for dozens of projects in lawmakers’ home districts.
